newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks start lower on consolidation.
newsitem.headline: French stocks start lower on consolidation.

text.p: The CAC index shed almost half a percent at the opening on Thursday as the market consolidated from yesterday's rise and reflected the Dow's 45-point fall overnight.
But traders said there was support around 2,602 on the index and as long as the dollar stayed strong, it was unlikely there would a big sell-off in French equities.
There were slim hopes of a slight easing by the Bank of France after today's policy meeting.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 8.29 points or 0.32 percent at 2,609.26 at 0811 GMT, after starting down 0.45 percent.
The CAC-40 April futures contract was down 13 at 2,607 from Wednesday's close.
PSA Peugeot Citroen bucks market, rises 1.13 percent to 629 francs. The carmaker may be benefiting from strong first quarter sales reported by Volkswagen, traders said.
Bic gains 0.7 percent to 864, supported by investor appetite for dollar earners.
Synthelabo up 3.04 percent at 645, adding to Wednesday's gains after bullish analysts meeting and upgrade.
Another stock in the pharmaceuticals sector, Sanofi, also rose, adding 0.75 percent to 539.
CCF gains 1.14 percent to 257.2, building on a correction of the last few days.
SEB rises 2.55 percent to 1,045. The appliance maker earlier said it had managed to get control of Brazil's Arno with 93.3 percent of voting rights for $153 million.
TF1 drops 1.9 percent to 567, on weak sentiment in the wake of reporting 1996 profits down 4.5 percent.
